statement: Tech shares had their worst week since 2020 as fears grew that huge AI spending will not pay off, and Nvidia fell sharply on Friday.
Gold fell to its lowest since September 2025 even while stocks crashed, and traders expect the Fed to raise rates in December.
The stock market's fear gauge will be lower on January 15, 2027 than at Friday's close near 36.
reasoning: The VIX closed near 36 on November 20 after the S&P 500 fell into a correction and Nvidia lost about 14 in a single day. Readings this high rarely last for weeks, because fear tends to fade once the selling slows, even when prices do not fully recover. I expect it well below 30 by mid-January. I am wrong if the VIX closes on January 15 above Friday's close, for example because the SEC look at Nvidia's accounting grows into a wider crisis or a Fed hike sets off another leg down.

statement: The US stock market (S&P 500) will close higher on June 30, 2027 than it closed on November 20, 2026.
reasoning: The S&P 500 closed November 20 more than 10 below its record, after a week of steep AI-driven losses and an expected Fed hike in December. Most corrections that stop short of a recession have recovered within seven months, and much of the bad news (the hike, Nvidia's troubles) is already in prices. I am wrong if the index ends June 2027 below Friday's close, for example because the Fed keeps raising rates into 2027 or the slump turns into a recession.

statement: The US dollar index will be higher on December 11, 2026 than at the November 20 close, after the Fed's December 8-9 meeting.
reasoning: After October's hot inflation report, traders put the odds of a Fed rate hike on December 8-9 at roughly 85 to 88, and Fed officials such as Waller have backed one. Higher US rates and a rush to safety during a stock slump both tend to lift the dollar. I am wrong if the dollar index is lower on December 11, for example because the Fed holds rates or signals that this hike is the last one, or because weak jobs data shift bets toward cuts.

statement: The dollar will buy fewer Japanese yen on December 31, 2026 than on November 20, 2026.
reasoning: The yen is near 160 per dollar even after close to 100 billion dollars of intervention. A Reuters poll found 86 of economists expect the Bank of Japan to raise rates to 1.50 at its December 17-18 meeting, and Governor Ueda says the bank should keep raising. A rate hike, a government ready to step in again and a nervous stock market all tend to strengthen the yen. I am wrong if the dollar buys more yen at year end than on November 20, for example because the Bank of Japan holds rates or the Fed's hike widens the gap between US and Japanese rates.

statement: The Nikkei 225 will close lower on December 18, 2026, the day of the Bank of Japan decision, than on November 20, 2026.
reasoning: The Nikkei fell about 7 over the past month. It faces higher interest rates at home and a shaky AI trade, which hurts Japan's chip and tech heavyweights. An expected Bank of Japan hike on December 17-18 and a stronger yen would weigh on exporters. I am wrong if the Nikkei closes December 18 above its November 20 close, for example because AI stocks bounce sharply or the Bank of Japan holds rates.

statement: Bitcoin will be cheaper on December 4, 2026 than on November 20, 2026.
reasoning: Bitcoin has fallen six weeks in a row and dipped below 62,000 dollars. US bitcoin funds have seen steady withdrawals, and an expected Fed rate hike plus a falling stock market keep risky assets under pressure. I expect the slide to go on for another two weeks. I am wrong if bitcoin is higher on December 4 than on November 20, for example because extreme fear brings in bargain hunters or money starts flowing back into the bitcoin funds.

statement: Coinbase shares will close lower on December 31, 2026 than on November 20, 2026.
reasoning: Coinbase closed at its lowest in about a year in mid-November and has lost about 30 in a month. Its third-quarter revenue fell 35 from a year earlier, and crypto prices are still falling while the stock market sells off and the Fed is expected to raise rates. I am wrong if Coinbase ends the year above its November 20 close, for example because bitcoin rebounds strongly in December.

statement: Brent crude oil will be cheaper on December 31, 2026 than its November 20 settlement near 92.57 dollars a barrel.
reasoning: Brent fell 4 last week as shipments through the Strait of Hormuz returned to roughly pre-war levels, after an earlier drop from above 116 dollars in October. Middle East output is rising, and a stock-market slump points to weaker demand. I am wrong if Brent ends the year above its November 20 settlement, for example because renewed attacks in the Iran war shut shipping again or OPEC+ cuts output at its November 29 meeting.

statement: US gasoline prices (UGA fund) will be lower on January 15, 2027 than on November 20, 2026.
reasoning: Crude oil is falling as Hormuz shipments return to normal, and US gasoline demand usually drops in mid-winter, when people drive less. Both should pull gasoline prices down into January. I am wrong if the fund ends higher on January 15, for example because the Iran war escalates again and crude jumps, or a refinery outage cuts supply.

statement: US homebuilder stocks (ITB) will close lower on December 31, 2026 than on November 20, 2026.
reasoning: Homebuilder confidence fell to 25 in November, its lowest since 2012, and fell in every region. The 30-year mortgage rate is above 7, and an expected Fed hike on December 8-9 keeps borrowing costs high while the stock market slides. I am wrong if ITB ends the year above its November 20 close, for example because long-term interest rates fall sharply as investors flee to safety and mortgage rates drop.

statement: The wheat fund will be cheaper on December 31, 2026 than on November 24, 2026, as plentiful harvests and a strong dollar keep pressing on prices.
reasoning: On November 18, wheat in Chicago fell about 4 in 100 in a day, the most of the three big crops, to about 5.70 dollars a bushel. Good weather in South America and large world supplies mean plenty of grain is coming. The dollar is at its highest in 19 months, which makes American wheat dearer for buyers abroad. We are wrong if wheat costs more at year end than on November 24, for example because fighting in the Black Sea region again threatens shipments from Ukraine and Russia, or a drought hurts the southern harvests.

statement: The interest rate on 10-year US government bonds will be higher on December 18, 2026 than on November 24, 2026, after the Fed's meeting of December 9 and 10.
reasoning: The 10-year rate has stayed above 5 in 100 through November, its highest in years, as prices kept rising faster than expected. Minutes of the Fed's October meeting say almost all its members expect to raise rates again, and traders give a December rise better than 9 chances in 10. We are wrong if the rate is lower on December 18, for example because the rise is already in the price and the Fed hints it will be the last, or a falling stock market sends savers into safe bonds.
